claims.text: Machine learning-guided optimization of thermal processing parameters can control phase evolution in Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni HEAs.
Optimized thermal processing will provide better kinetic control of diffusion and nucleation events.
Better kinetic control will produce a more reproducible microstructure with a larger fraction of desired phases and fewer unintended transformations.
Conventionally cast and heat-treated Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni HEAs exhibit mixed, poorly controlled phase distributions.
Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni2.1 specimens can be subjected to isothermal aging at selected temperatures and holding times followed by rapid quenching.
Relevant aging temperatures for this alloy system span 520 to 1200 degrees Celsius.
Holding time can be varied as a thermal-processing parameter in this alloy system.
Cooling rates can be optimized as part of the proposed thermal treatment.
A machine learning model trained on prior phase-evolution data can select the annealing temperature, holding time, and cooling rate.
Tailored thermal profiles modify the nucleation and growth kinetics governing phase transformations.
Fine-tuning diffusion and nucleation kinetics stabilizes target phases such as ordered precipitates.
Fine-tuning diffusion and nucleation kinetics suppresses undesired phase transformations in this multicomponent HEA.
Machine learning-optimized treatment will increase the fraction and uniformity of desired phases relative to conventional thermal profiles.
The optimized treatment will improve related mechanical properties relative to conventional treatment.
Benefits are expected only within an experimentally validated thermal-parameter range because other kinetic limitations may dominate outside that range.
